MASTER PROMPT — WASL ARENA

MASTER PROMPT — WASL ARENA

ADU 6th Annual COE STEM Programming with AI Competition — Cycle 3

Act as an elite multidisciplinary team comprising:

- 
Senior AI and computer vision engineer

- 
Full-stack software architect

- 
Python/FastAPI backend engineer

- 
React/TypeScript frontend engineer

- 
AI evaluation and quality assurance specialist

- 
Premium UI/UX and creative director

- 
Scientific and technical report writer

- 
Competition presentation strategist

- 
Cinematic video director and scriptwriter

- 
GitHub, Vercel, and backend deployment specialist

Your assignment is to independently execute the development and submission-production workflow for WASL Arena — The Family AI Games Championship.

You must strictly adhere to the attached official Abu Dhabi University challenge brief and all submission requirements.

The target is the Cycle 3 Track (Grades 9–12), not the Advanced Champions Track.

There must be exactly three games: football plus two original games.

PART I — COMPETITION DEFINITION

1. Official challenge

Competition: 6th Annual COE STEM Programming with AI Competition

Theme: AI for Family

Problem: Family AI Game Day

Track: Cycle 3 — Grades 9–12

The challenge requires a working application that hosts family games inspired by culture, heritage or sports.

The human host sets up players and teams, explains rules, controls gameplay and manages rounds.

The AI observes actual gameplay through video and audio, detects relevant events, applies predefined rules and generates verifiable results.

2. Mandatory functionality

The solution must:

- 
Include football and exactly two original games.

- 
Support team and individual competition.

- 
Allow families to choose their game.

- 
Register players and teams.

- 
Define points, timers, turns, rounds, penalties, ties and winners.

- 
Accept uploaded gameplay videos with audio.

- 
Support direct camera and microphone recording.

- 
Analyze actual game footage.

- 
Generate AI judgments grounded in observed evidence.

- 
Explain how judgments were made.

- 
Apply verified AI results to scores.

- 
Display final scores, winners and MVP information where relevant.

- 
Demonstrate actual gameplay and AI judging in the student video.

- 
Provide a working, accessible, publicly deployed prototype.

Do not use the example original games shown in the problem statement.

The application must not depend on prerecorded animations or fabricated AI judgments.

PART II — THE CONCEPT

3. Product identity

Name: WASL Arena

Tagline: One family. Three games. One fair AI referee.

Core proposition: Transform family gaming into a connected experience where artificial intelligence watches, listens, judges and explains.

The innovation is the combination of:

- 
Real physical games

- 
Computer vision

- 
Speech and audio recognition

- 
Rule-based intelligence

- 
Transparent scoring

- 
UAE cultural relevance

- 
Family interaction

- 
Explainable AI

WASL Arena is not a collection of digital minigames.

The family plays in the real world, while the application operates as the game host, observer, referee and championship manager.

4. The signature innovation

AI REFEREE REPLAY

Every AI scoring decision must have an evidence trail.

For example:

Decision: Goal awarded to Team A.

Evidence: Video timestamp, detected player, tracked ball and observed goal-line crossing.

Rule: Football Rule F-03.

Score change: Team A +1.

Status: Verified or requires human review.

The user must be able to inspect the moment that produced the judgment.

Create an evidence timeline with playable video segments, frame annotations, detection outputs and explanations.

This is the centerpiece of the project's technical identity and competition presentation.

PART III — THE THREE GAMES

GAME 1 — FOOTBALL AI

Concept

A real family football match monitored by an AI referee.

Mode

Team versus team.

Default: Two players per team.

Features

- 
Player registration

- 
Team assignment

- 
Team-color identification

- 
Numbered player identification where feasible

- 
Video recording and upload

- 
Player and ball detection

- 
Motion tracking

- 
Goal detection

- 
Score updates

- 
Possession estimates

- 
Match timer

- 
Tie-break rules

- 
MVP calculation

- 
Evidence replay

Technical implementation

Use OpenCV, suitable object detection models and temporal tracking.

The initial demonstrable setup should use:

- 
A clearly marked mini-football playing area

- 
Two visible goals

- 
Contrasting team bibs

- 
Large readable player identifiers

- 
A bright, visually detectable football

- 
A stable camera angle

Analyze frames to locate players, the ball and calibrated goal regions.

Detect goal events by tracking the ball across the relevant goal boundary over consecutive frames.

Do not generate a goal merely because a language model describes one.

Compute a possession proxy using observed player/ball proximity when tracking data is reliable.

If a player, ball or goal event cannot be confidently distinguished, mark the event as unresolved.

Scoring

- 
Verified goal: +1

- 
Invalid goal: 0

- 
Match winner: Highest score

- 
Tie: Golden-goal extension or configured tie-break

- 
MVP: Calculated from verified individual contributions only

Clearly distinguish measured possession from estimates.

GAME 2 — FALAJ FLOW

Concept

An AI-observed collaborative irrigation challenge inspired by traditional Emirati falaj systems.

Families compete to construct an efficient water distribution network.

Mode

Team versus team.

Physical setup

Use a printable 5×5 board with:

- 
A water-source tile

- 
Three agricultural destinations

- 
Fixed obstacles

- 
Connectable water-channel tiles

- 
Distinctive printed visual markers

Players physically position and rotate channel tiles.

The objective

Connect the water source to as many destinations as possible while avoiding obstacles and invalid paths.

AI features

- 
Board calibration

- 
Tile identification

- 
Tile orientation detection

- 
Real-time or recorded board-state extraction

- 
Route visualization

- 
Graph construction

- 
Connectivity verification

- 
Invalid-path detection

- 
Automatic scoring

Technical reasoning

Convert the observed tile arrangement into a graph.

Represent valid water connections as edges.

Use graph traversal to determine which agricultural destinations are reachable from the water source.

Reject paths blocked by obstacles or invalid tile orientation.

Scoring

- 
Valid destination reached: +3

- 
Invalid outlet or leak: -1

- 
Completion-time bonus: Up to +2

- 
Round duration: 90 seconds

- 
Tie-break: Shortest valid network, then completion time

Visual wow factor

Display the physical board on one side and its AI-generated digital network on the other.

Animate verified water flow through the reconstructed graph.

Water must only flow through routes validated by actual observed placements.

GAME 3 — SOUQ SIGNAL

Concept

A family marketplace challenge combining object recognition, speech recognition, budgeting and logical reasoning.

The family receives a shopping mission and must complete it using physical item cards.

Mode

Individual competition, with optional alternating players.

Physical setup

Create a printable card collection containing:

- 
Dates

- 
Saffron

- 
Coffee

- 
Textiles

- 
Spices

- 
Pottery

Each item has:

- 
A unique visual identifier

- 
A fixed game price

- 
English and Arabic labels

Gameplay

The application generates a shopping mission.

Example:

"Purchase the dates, coffee and pottery within a budget of 15 dirhams."

The player selects cards, presents them to the camera and verbally announces the items.

The AI compares:

- 
The requested shopping list

- 
The visually observed cards

- 
The recognized spoken selections

- 
The total item cost

- 
The remaining budget

Technical implementation

Use visual markers for reliable card identification.

Use speech transcription for spoken selections.

Match recognized words to a fixed bilingual item vocabulary.

Do not rely on open-ended language-model judgment to determine whether a purchase is valid.

Scoring

- 
Correct requested item: +2

- 
Verified agreement between spoken and visually observed item: +1

- 
Budget exceeded: -2

- 
Duplicate item: No additional item points

- 
Tie-break: Lowest valid expenditure, then completion time

Visual wow factor

Show the live camera feed beside:

- 
AI-recognized products

- 
Speech transcript

- 
Shopping basket

- 
Budget calculation

- 
Rule validation

- 
Automated score explanation

Use a prominent visual indicator when audio and video evidence agree.

If either input is ambiguous, request review instead of issuing an unsupported penalty.

21. What you must do now

Begin with a concise, concrete architecture and implementation specification for WASL Arena.

Then proceed directly to development.

Do not stop after brainstorming or creating a plan.

Implement and validate the application first, then use the actual implementation to generate the technical report, presentation and video materials.

At every stage, distinguish completed work from pending work.

If any external action requires authorization, such as publishing to GitHub, deploying a service or supplying API credentials, identify it explicitly and continue all independent work.

The final product must be technically credible, visually outstanding and unmistakably aligned with the Cycle 3 Family AI Game Day competition.

Our objective is to deliver the strongest possible competition entry through originality, functional intelligence, transparent judging, exceptional user experience and verifiable technical evidence.

My final strategic recommendations

1. Prioritize the AI referee over visual complexity.

A real five-second clip producing a correct, explainable judgment is more persuasive than a polished interface with simulated results.

2. Record genuine gameplay early.

Football, Falaj Flow and Souq Signal each need at least one usable recording. These recordings will support the prototype, tests, report, presentation and video simultaneously.

3. Build the five submission items from the same verified evidence.

Use the same screenshots, architecture, test results and AI-referee decisions across the technical report, thirty-slide presentation and two-minute demonstration.

My verdict: WASL Arena with Football AI, Falaj Flow and Souq Signal is the strongest direction I recommend for your updated Cycle 3 challenge. It combines sports, Emirati heritage, visual intelligence, multimodal AI and explainable scoring within exactly three games. Its winning potential will depend on whether the actual video-based judging works reliably during the demonstration.

GAME 2: FALAJ FLOW

Mode: Team versus team.

Create a physical strategy challenge inspired by traditional UAE irrigation.

Players construct a water-channel network using printed tiles on a 5×5 board.

The AI identifies the tile positions and orientations, reconstructs the network as a graph and verifies whether water can reach three agricultural destinations.

AI capabilities

- 
Visual board recognition

- 
Tile-position detection

- 
Graph construction

- 
Route validation

- 
Obstacle detection

- 
Automated scoring

- 
Animated, evidence-backed water-flow visualization

Rules

- 
Connected destination: +3

- 
Invalid outlet/leak: -1

- 
Time bonus: Up to +2

- 
Round duration: 90 seconds

- 
Tie-break: Shortest valid network, then time

Wow factor: Split-screen physical board and live digital reconstruction, with verified water flowing across the graph.
